# NetCage

> A per-app firewall for Android. Choose an enabled, installed app that requests internet access
> and close its route on Wi-Fi and mobile.

NetCage is an Android application, package `com.aoneahsan.netcage`, prepared for release on Google Play, not yet published.
This site is its documentation. It is prerendered, so every page's HTML already contains its full
text — no JavaScript is needed to read it. The Markdown source is public at
https://github.com/aoneahsan/netcage-docs under `docs/`, where the page at `/<name>` is
`docs/<name>.md`.

## How it works, in one paragraph

Android lets a `VpnService` route selected apps. NetCage builds an on-device tunnel and adds caged
packages to its allow-list. Android applies VPN routing by UID, so apps sharing a selected package's
UID enter the tunnel too. NetCage examines IP and transport headers in memory to address a TCP reset
or ICMP port-unreachable response. It does not inspect payloads or hostnames, keep a traffic log, or
forward caged traffic. Apps outside caged Android UIDs do not enter the tunnel. Android still runs a
foreground VPN service while a cage is active, so NetCage does not promise an exact zero resource cost.

## What NetCage is not

- **Not an ad blocker.** It does no domain filtering, no hosts file, no DNS interception, and no
  content blocking of any kind. It blocks an app, entirely or not at all.
- **Not a packet-content inspector.** Refusing a caged app's connection needs destination and
  transport-header fields. Packet payloads and hostnames are not inspected, and no DNS, URL or traffic
  log is kept.
- **Not a proxy or a real VPN.** The tunnel has no server on the other end. That is the mechanism.
